title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 4.5 Responsibility: Personal and school items

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Responsibility means taking care of what has been entrusted to you. In this sub-strand you will name personal items and school property, learn the use of each one, and practise caring for them so that they last and other learners can use them well.

## Strand 4.0: Christian Values
Sub-strand 4.5: Responsibility: Personal and school items
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify personal items and how they care for them
b) identify school properties and how they care for them
c) acquire responsibility by taking care of personal and school properties

## Key inquiry questions
1. How do you take care of personal and school items?

## Core competencies
• Communication: the skill of communication and self-expression is exhibited as learners compose a poem.

## Values
• Responsibility: learners care for personal and school items.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Health Issues: Personal hygiene is portrayed as learners practise taking care of personal property.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose a poem.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Christian Values, Sub-strand 4.5 Responsibility: Personal and school items

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Caring for personal items

LESSON 1: CARING FOR PERSONAL ITEMS
===================================

## What you will learn
• Identify personal items and the use of each one.
• Explain how to take good care of personal items.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify personal items and how they care for them; c) acquire responsibility by taking care of personal and school properties

## Introduction
A pullover, a pen, a pencil, an eraser, an exercise book and a textbook are personal items. They help you learn. A responsible learner knows what each item is for and keeps it in good condition.

## Notes
### Personal items and their uses
Personal items belong to you. Your parents or guardians, or sometimes the school, provided them so that you can learn and stay well. Displaying them helps you remember what you have.

- A pullover keeps you warm on a cold morning.
- A pen is used for writing in ink.
- Pencils are used for drawing and for work that may need rubbing out.
- An eraser removes pencil marks so that you can correct a mistake neatly.
- Exercise books hold your class work, homework and notes.
- Textbooks hold the lessons you read in class.

Other personal items include the school uniform, shoes, a bag and a drinking bottle. Each one has a use. A bag carries the books. Shoes protect the feet. The uniform identifies you as a learner of your school.

### How to care for them
- Write your name in your books so that a lost book can be returned.
- Do not tear pages or scribble over the work.
- Keep pens closed and sharpen pencils over a bin.
- Wash the pullover when it is dirty, fold it, and do not drag it on the ground.
- Pack the bag so that books are not bent by a water bottle.
- Keep items dry. Do not leave books in the rain.
- Do not lend an item and then forget who has it.
- Put each item back in the bag when the lesson ends.

### Why care is a Christian duty
These items cost money. If they are lost or broken, someone must replace them, and you may miss learning while you wait. Taking care of them is responsibility. A responsible person looks after what he or she has been given, even when the teacher is not watching. Personal cleanliness is part of this care: a clean uniform, clean hands and a tidy bag help you stay healthy.

Before you leave school, check: pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books, textbooks and pullover. The check takes a short time and saves a long search at home.

## Key words
• personal item — something that belongs to you and is for your own use
• responsibility — the duty to look after what you have been given
• property — things that belong to a person or to a school

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner leaves an exercise book on the field and the rain wets it. The writing cannot be read. What should have been done?

Working:
1. An exercise book is a personal item used for class work.
2. Books must be kept dry and packed in the bag.
3. Leaving it outside does not care for it.

Answer: The book should have been closed and packed in the bag before the learner went to play.

## Activity: Display personal items and say their uses
You will need: Pullover, pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books and textbooks, Exercise book for notes
1. Display your personal items on the desk, for example a pullover, pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books and textbooks.
2. In pairs, list the use of each item.
3. Say why you should take good care of your personal items.
4. Write two lines of a poem on taking care of personal property.

## Practice
1. Name four personal items a learner uses at school.
2. What is the use of an eraser, and what is the use of a textbook?
3. Give three ways of caring for exercise books.
4. Why should a Christian learner care for personal items?

## Summary
• Personal items include a pullover, pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books and textbooks.
• Each item has a use, so it should be named, packed and kept clean and dry.
• Looking after them is part of Christian responsibility.

### Answers to practice
1. Any four, for example pullover, pen, pencil, eraser, exercise book and textbook.
2. An eraser removes pencil marks. A textbook is read for the lesson.
3. Any three: write your name in them, do not tear pages, keep them dry, pack them in the bag, and do not scribble over the work.
4. It is an act of responsibility. The items cost money, and caring for them helps the learner keep learning.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Caring for school property

LESSON 2: CARING FOR SCHOOL PROPERTY
====================================

## What you will learn
• Identify school property and how to care for it.
• Explain why learners share the duty of looking after school items.

Curriculum outcomes: b) identify school properties and how they care for them; c) acquire responsibility by taking care of personal and school properties

## Introduction
The desk you sit on, the textbook the teacher lends out, and the tap in the school yard do not belong to one learner. They are school property. Everyone who uses them has a duty to care for them.

## Notes
### What school property is
School property belongs to the school and is shared by many learners. It includes desks and chairs, the classroom and its windows and doors, the chalkboard, textbooks and readers that the school owns, charts on the wall, the library books, balls and other games equipment, the toilets, water taps, the fence and the playing field.

A textbook that the school gave you for the year is still school property. You use it, but you do not own it. At the end of the time set by the school it goes back, ready for another learner.

### How to care for school property
- Sit on the chair properly. Do not swing on it or break the joints.
- Do not write or carve names on desks, walls or textbooks.
- Do not bang doors or throw stones at windows.
- Use the chalkboard only when the teacher asks you to.
- Cover a borrowed textbook, keep it dry, and return it on the day you are told.
- Put litter in the bin so that the compound stays clean.
- Close a tap after you drink, so water is not wasted.
- Use the toilet properly and leave it clean for the next person.
- Report a broken desk, a leaking tap or a torn book to the teacher instead of hiding the damage.

### Why this care matters
When one learner breaks a window or tears a shared book, the whole class suffers. Money that could buy more books is used for repairs. Learning stops while a desk is being mended. Caring for school property is responsibility, and it helps learners live together in peace. Christians show this value even when no teacher is in the room, because doing right does not depend on being watched.

Personal items and school items are cared for in the same spirit: know what the item is, use it for its proper work, keep it clean, put it back, and report damage. A poem, a class monitor and a tidy cupboard are all ways of practising this every day.

## Key words
• school property — things that belong to the school and are shared by learners
• damage — harm done to an item so that it cannot be used well
• report — to tell the teacher when something is broken or lost

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Learners find a school textbook with pages missing and names written across the maps. What is wrong, and what should the class do?

Working:
1. The textbook is school property.
2. Writing on it and tearing pages is not caring for it.
3. Damage should be reported, and the class should agree on how borrowed books will be kept.

Answer: The book was misused. Tell the teacher, stop writing in school books, and return books in good condition.

## Activity: Poem on personal and school property
You will need: Manila paper, Pencils
1. In pairs, list school properties you use and the use of each one.
2. Say why you should take good care of both personal and school items.
3. Compose a short poem on taking care of personal and school properties and read it to the class.
4. Walk round the classroom and put chairs, books and litter in the right places.

## Practice
1. Name four things that are school property.
2. How should a learner care for a textbook that belongs to the school?
3. Why does damaging a desk affect other learners?
4. What should you do if you find a broken window or a leaking tap?

## Summary
• School property is shared. It includes furniture, books, buildings, taps and play equipment.
• Do not write on or break shared things. Return borrowed books and report damage.
• Responsibility means caring for both personal items and school property.

### Answers to practice
1. Any four, for example desks, chairs, windows, school textbooks, the chalkboard, taps, toilets, library books or balls.
2. Cover it, do not tear or write on the pages, keep it dry, and return it when the school asks.
3. The desk is shared. Others cannot sit well, and the school must spend money on repairs.
4. Report it to the teacher. Do not hide the damage.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.5 RESPONSIBILITY: PERSONAL AND SCHOOL ITEMS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these is a personal item?
   A. The classroom window
   B. Your exercise book
   C. The school tap
   D. The staffroom door

2. What is a pencil used for?
   A. Keeping warm
   B. Writing and drawing
   C. Closing a tap
   D. Covering a window

3. Which pair shows good care of personal items?
   A. Leaving books in the rain and tearing pages
   B. Writing your name in books and packing them in the bag
   C. Lending every book and forgetting who has it
   D. Dragging the pullover on the ground

4. Why should a pullover be washed and folded?

5. Which of these is school property?
   A. Your own pen
   B. A desk in the classroom
   C. Your pullover
   D. Your eraser

6. A school textbook is different from your exercise book because:
   A. It has no pages
   B. It belongs to the school and should be returned in good condition
   C. Only teachers may see it
   D. It does not need care

7. What should learners do when they finish using a water tap?
   A. Leave it running
   B. Close it
   C. Hide the tap
   D. Break the handle

8. You accidentally crack a desk. What is the responsible action?

9. Give one reason why Christians should care for personal and school items.

10. Name one personal item and one school item, and say how you will care for each this week.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.5 RESPONSIBILITY: PERSONAL AND SCHOOL ITEMS
========================================

1. B. Your exercise book
   An exercise book belongs to the learner and is used for that learner's work.

2. B. Writing and drawing
   Pencils are personal items used for writing and drawing.

3. B. Writing your name in books and packing them in the bag
   A name helps a lost book to be returned, and packing keeps books safe.

4. It is a personal item that keeps you warm. Washing and folding keep it clean and ready to wear.
   Caring for clothes is part of looking after personal property and personal hygiene.

5. B. A desk in the classroom
   Desks belong to the school and are used by many learners.

6. B. It belongs to the school and should be returned in good condition
   You use a school textbook, but it remains school property.

7. B. Close it
   Closing the tap cares for school property and does not waste water.

8. Tell the teacher. Do not hide the damage.
   Reporting damage is part of caring for school property.

9. It is an act of responsibility. The items help learning, they cost money, and school items are shared.
   Responsibility is the value taught in this sub-strand.

10. Personal: any item such as a pen or book, kept clean, named or packed. School: any item such as a desk or tap, not damaged, and damage reported.
   The learner should show care for both kinds of property.
